analysis:
Both files in this batch (docs/architecture/inference.md and docs/developer/test.md) are documentation-only. I examined the supplied head text (inference.md lines 4924-5333 and 5334-5490) and the test.md patch. Both describe Gemma routed-expert checks, Gemma pipeline default lanes, and the Qwen27 TP media, native-context, assistant, and cluster-runtime-facts mechanisms. No executable code, configuration, or control changed in this batch, so no security regression is introduced by these edits.

The statements most relevant to the threat model are conservative. They say the media transport and pricing patches enable no capability, readiness or model qualification. They say encoded media is held only by the owner and rank 0. They say prefix reuse is disabled for the Qwen media ingress path, which is consistent with T-041 cross-tenant cache concerns and with scope containing the media fingerprint. They say a pair-serving grant gates coordinator sessions and that qualification evidence is still required. The docs also say a setup saved for coordinator pairing carries no speculation.

Remaining integration questions are about code outside this batch: Gemma pipeline default lanes (DistributedInstalledPlan.gemma4PipelineBatchLanes), the lane and tenant partitioning behind multi-lane serving, the prefix-cache partitioning that the docs reference, and the Qwen27 native-context memory charge (QwenTensorParallelRequestCharge) with its 503 refusal behavior. These cannot be verified from the docs alone. The patch excerpts are truncated, but the changed ranges are marked complete, and the displayed content shows only documentation. No threat-model update is needed from these edits.
